name: Hol's der Geier
description: Hol's der Geier (Beat the Buzzard) is a quick-fire tactical bidding game designed by the legendary Alex Randolph. Players compete to capture 'Mouse' cards (positive points) while avoiding 'Vulture' cards (negative points). It is famous for its simple ruleset that yields surprisingly deep psychological gameplay and second-guessing.

content.text: Hol's der Geier (Beat the Buzzard) is a quick-fire tactical bidding game designed by the legendary Alex Randolph. Players compete to capture 'Mouse' cards (positive points) while avoiding 'Vulture' cards (negative points). It is famous for its simple ruleset that yields surprisingly deep psychological gameplay and second-guessing.
Designed by Alex Randolph and first published by Ravensburger in 1988. It has been released under multiple titles including 'Stupide Vautour' (France) and 'Beat the Buzzard' (UK).
The 15 prize cards (10 Mice valued +1 to +10, 5 Vultures valued -1 to -5) are shuffled and placed face-down.

items.text: Animal theme variants: In some editions vultures are replaced with cats (e.g. Il Gioco dei Gatti) or mice with meerkats (Chinese version). Rules unchanged.
Combined tie prize: When all players tie or all valid bids are cancelled, the prize card stays in the centre and its value is added to the next revealed prize.
Player count: Best with 2; playable with 2 to 5. Each player always has 15 bidding cards; with fewer than 5 players some sets are unused.
